# Test failures expected on every CI platform, as CLASS/TEST, matched case
# insensitively. Read .github/known-test-failures/README.md before adding to
# any file in this directory.

# ReadMe.first records these as failing whenever the suite's output is
# redirected. A hosted runner has no console at all, so they cannot pass
# anywhere in CI. Confirmed failing for this reason on Windows, Linux and macOS.
CHAROUT.testGroup/TEST_STDOUT_START
LINEOUT.testGroup/TEST_LINE_TRANSIENT

# Timing tests that assert an *upper* bound on how long something took. A sleep
# interval is a floor, not a ceiling; no sleep API promises to return promptly,
# and a shared virtual machine cannot offer real-time scheduling. Observed:
#
#   macOS    SysSleep(1.333) took 1.360999, allowed 1.333 to 1.359
#   macOS    SysSleep(1.333) took 1.403189, allowed 1.333 to 1.359
#   macOS    SysSleep(0.016) took 0.14777,  allowed 0.016 to 0.042
#   Windows  SysSleep(1.333) took 1.367,    allowed 1.312 to 1.363
#
# These started in the macOS list and moved here once Windows produced the same
# failure, so this is two platforms observed rather than an assumption that it
# would happen everywhere. They are flaky rather than deterministic: an entry
# here permits a failure, it does not require one, so runs where the scheduler
# behaves stay green.
#
# Worth raising upstream. A test that cannot pass on a busy machine is testing
# the machine, not the interpreter, and the 0.016 case overshot its 26 ms
# tolerance by more than 100 ms.
SYSSLEEP.testGroup/TEST_SLEEP_CONCURRENT
SYSSLEEP.testGroup/TEST_SLEEP_DURATION
